title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 7 Coordinate Geometry (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2023-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (negative allowed). No calculator.

patterns.T1: Distance / from origin / from an axis

S1.name: Distance formula; from the origin and the axes
S1.tip: PQ = √[(x2 − x1)² + (y2 − y1)²]. From the origin √(x² + y²). Distance from the x-axis is |y|, from the y-axis |x|.

S2.name: Distance with letters, trig or surds
S2.tip: Square the differences, expand, and use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; the cross terms usually cancel.

S3.name: Type of figure; collinear points
S3.tip: Right triangle: Pythagoras on the squared sides. Collinear: two distances add up to the third. Square: equal sides AND equal diagonals.

S4.name: Equidistant points
S4.tip: Equidistant: set PA² = PB² (no roots). A point on the x-axis is (x, 0), on the y-axis (0, y). Keep both roots unless a condition rules one out.

S5.name: Section formula: point in a given ratio
S5.tip: Section formula: ((m1x2 + m2x1)/(m1 + m2), (m1y2 + m2y1)/(m1 + m2)). m1 goes with the SECOND point. PR = 2RQ means 2 : 1.

S6.name: Find the ratio (axis shortcut)
S6.tip: Take the ratio k : 1 and use one coordinate. x-axis → y = 0 → ratio −y1 : y2; y-axis → x = 0 → ratio −x1 : x2.

S7.name: Mid-point, trisection, four equal parts
S7.tip: Mid-point = average of the coordinates. Trisection: ratios 1 : 2 and 2 : 1. Four equal parts: mid-point, then mid-points of the halves.

S8.name: Mid-point uses: parallelogram, median, circle
S8.tip: Parallelogram: diagonals share a mid-point → D = A + C − B. Median: mid-point of the opposite side, then distance. Circle centre = mid-point of a diameter.

S9.name: Lines parallel to the axes; A-R checks
S9.tip: Parallel to the x-axis: y = constant; parallel to the y-axis: x = constant. A point on the x-axis is 0 from the x-axis.

questions.question: A(1, 2), B(4, 3), C(6, 6) and D(p, 5) are the vertices of a parallelogram taken in order. Find p.
questions.explanation: Mid-point of AC = (7/2, 4) = mid-point of BD = ((4 + p)/2, 4) → p = 3.
